urteile.grund: Composite holding the personal data of the first applicant. It gets the person container eCH-0044 personIdentification, which exists verbatim in the catalogue (id 809). This matches the corpus practice for «Personalien GesuchstellerIn/Gesuchsteller/in» (more than 25 rows). Its 9 parts are judged one by one. Nothing on this form is 'propagiert', so 'korrekt' cannot apply.
Current official surname of applicant 1 → eCH-0044 personIdentificationType/officialName. Checked to exist verbatim.
First name of applicant 1 → eCH-0044 personIdentificationType/firstName.

This is a past name, so officialName (the current value) is excluded. Searched the catalogue for every past-name element (former/previous/original/alliance/birth/maiden): the only candidates are originalName (eCH-0011/0044/0084/0213/0228, the Ledigname) and allianceName (a name used jointly with the partner, not a past name). originalName is the closest fit and matches the corpus practice for Ledigname, Geburtsname and lediger Name (11×). The name a person may return to after dissolution is the Ledigname (PartG Art. 30a). Caveat: if the person was married before and kept that married name, the name before registration differs from the Ledigname.
Date of birth of applicant 1 → eCH-0044 personIdentificationType/dateOfBirth.
Occupation as free text → eCH-0021 jobDataType/jobTitle (corpus practice for «Beruf»: 22×).

Place of origin, or the home country for foreign nationals → eCH-0011 placeOfOriginType/originName. The corpus does the same for «Heimatort / Land» (8×) and «Heimatort/Staatsangehörigkeit» (4×). Caveat: the label bundles two data items. For a foreign national, the country would be eCH-0011 nationalityData/countryInfo/country (a candidate for the «aufteilen» naming check).

On the form, «Wohnadresse» is its own line above a separate «Ort» line, so it holds street and house number → eCH-0010 addressInformationType/street (corpus 6×). It is not the container eCH-0011 dwellingAddress, because the place is a separate part. The house number would be eCH-0010 houseNumber.
Place of residence in the address block → eCH-0010 addressInformationType/town (corpus 55×).
Telephone number of applicant 1 → eCH-0046 phoneType/phoneNumber (corpus 182×).

The datum is the language into which applicant 1 must be interpreted at the court hearing. It is a text value, not a yes/no box. Searched every language, translation and interpreter element in the 290-standard catalogue: languageOfCorrespondance (eCH-0011/0021/0045/0098/0116/0148/0173/0201/0228/0244/0246/0258/0260), eCH-0108 correspondenceLanguage, eCH-0261 preferredCorrespondenceLanguage, eCH-0084/0085/0086/0213/0214 response/descriptionLanguage, eCH-0260 nativeLanguage/firstLanguage/examLanguage/schoolLanguage/formLanguage, and the language elements of eCH-0108/0129/0155/0206/0228/0239/0252/0258/0259. None defines an interpreter or hearing language. languageOfCorrespondance is the language of written correspondence, and the court keeps writing in German. Also checked the justice standards: eCH-0051 V3.0.0 (Polizei und Justiz) has no elements in the catalogue, and its main document defines only base types (languageType = ISO 639 code), no interpreter datum. eCH-0136 (Zivilstand responsibilities) and eCH-0307 (Justizvollzug, In Arbeit, no elements) do not fit either.

Composite holding the personal data of the second applicant, an equal party to the joint request → eCH-0044 personIdentification (corpus practice for Personalien composites). Its 8 parts are judged one by one; unlike applicant 1, no name before registration is asked.
Current official surname of applicant 2 → eCH-0044 personIdentificationType/officialName.
First name of applicant 2 → eCH-0044 personIdentificationType/firstName.
Date of birth of applicant 2 → eCH-0044 personIdentificationType/dateOfBirth.
Occupation as free text → eCH-0021 jobDataType/jobTitle (corpus practice 22×).

Place of origin, or the home country for foreign nationals → eCH-0011 placeOfOriginType/originName, as the corpus does for «Heimatort / Land». Caveat: the label bundles two data items. A foreign national's country would be eCH-0011 nationalityData/countryInfo/country.
«Wohnadresse» is its own line above a separate «Ort» line, so it holds street and house number → eCH-0010 addressInformationType/street. The house number would be eCH-0010 houseNumber.
Place of residence in the address block → eCH-0010 addressInformationType/town.
Telephone number of applicant 2 → eCH-0046 phoneType/phoneNumber.

Same datum as for applicant 1: the language for interpreting at the hearing. The same full-catalogue search found nothing that fits. That search covered every languageOfCorrespondance, correspondenceLanguage and preferredCorrespondenceLanguage element, the response/descriptionLanguage elements, eCH-0260 native/first/exam/school/formLanguage and every other language element. eCH-0051 (Justiz) has only an ISO-639 languageType and no data element; eCH-0136 and eCH-0307 do not fit. No element defines an interpreter or hearing language, and languageOfCorrespondance means written correspondence, a different datum.

The date of registration is the start date of the status «in eingetragener Partnerschaft» (code 6). That status still applies, because dissolution is only being requested, so this is not a past or changed value. eCH-0011 has exactly this in maritalDataRestrictedPartnershipType/dateOfMaritalStatus, and eCH-0020 eventPartnership carries it as maritalInfo/maritalData/dateOfMaritalStatus. The corpus maps «Datum der Heirat / Eintragung der Partnerschaft» the same way (form 290).

Place where the partnership was registered → eCH-0021 maritalDataAddonType/placeOfMarriage. The XSD confirms that eCH-0020 eventPartnership uses maritalInfoRestrictedMarriageType, and that type contains this very maritalDataAddon. The element therefore holds the place of the partnership registration as well.

Date on which applicant 1 signed. Two signatories sign separately, so this is a date per signature. eCH-0058 messageDate and eventDate are message-header values, one per message, and cannot hold two different signing dates. eCH-0119 locationAndDate is tied to the tax-return attachments (attachedForms/listOfSecurities). eCH-0039 openingDate and eCH-0260 signatures (apprenticeship-contract booleans) do not fit. The signature standards eCH-0091/0220/0230/0250/0274/0282 have no elements. This is consistent with the reviewed practice «Ort und Datum» → kein_standard (eSH-0001 placeAndDate).

Handwritten signature. Searched every sign/signature element: eCH-0039 signer is only the signer's name as a token. eCH-0260 signatures/…SignatureConfirmation are booleans for apprenticeship contracts. eCH-0091/0220/0230/0250/0274/0282 concern electronic signatures and have no elements. The reviewed corpus practice for «Unterschrift» is kein_standard (propagated from 15, 29 reviewed rows; eSH-0001 signature).

Signing date of applicant 2, a date per signature. The message-level eCH-0058 messageDate/eventDate cannot hold two different signing dates. eCH-0119 locationAndDate belongs to tax-return attachments, and eCH-0039 openingDate and eCH-0260 signatures do not fit. The signature standards have no elements, so there is no element in the catalogue.

Handwritten signature of applicant 2. Same search as for applicant 1: eCH-0039 signer, eCH-0260 signatures, and eCH-0091/0220/0230/0250/0274/0282, which have no elements. No standard element exists; the reviewed corpus practice is kein_standard (eSH-0001).

A party living abroad must name a person in Switzerland to whom the court delivers documents. That is the party's delivery address via a third person. eCH-0011 personType/contactData (contactDataType) holds exactly that, according to the XSD: optionally personIdentification, personIdentificationPartner or partnerIdOrganisation, plus a mandatory contactAddress. It is the container, because the single text field holds both the person and the address. Corpus practice maps «Zustelladresse» to contactAddress (5×). eCH-0119 representativePerson (used once for «Zustellbevollmächtigter (Personalien)») belongs to the tax-return mainForm and fits a court proceeding less well.

A single attachment field for the documents listed in the Merkblatt. The form does not itemise them, so this is not a checklist. → container element eCH-0058 headerType/attachment, the enclosures transported with the submission (xs:anyType, unbounded). The corpus maps «Unterlagen zu den finanziellen Verhältnissen» and 6 single «Beilagen» fields the same way. The kein_standard practice for «Beilagen» covers multiselect checklists of named documents, which is not the shape of this field.
